turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come through. I've done your observations, and your partner's still outside if you want him later. Blood pressure was one eighteen over seventy two, pulse eighty eight, temperature thirty six point eight, and your oxygen was ninety eight on air.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks, that's helpful. I'm Dr Ellis. Have a seat. What's brought you in today?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Um, I'm pregnant, and I've got spotting, and these cramps. I don't know, doctor. It's really scared me.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): I can hear that. How many weeks do you think you are?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): The last period was around Diwali, or after. I can't pin the day down. Maybe eight weeks, maybe ten. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): So I'll take that as dates unclear, last period around Diwali or a little after, perhaps eight to ten weeks. When did the spotting actually start?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): I've been feeling really sick in the mornings, can't face breakfast at all. And my sister won't stop texting.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll come back to the sickness in a moment. The spotting, when did that begin?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Oh. Um, Wednesday. No, wait, Thursday. About four days, I think. I don't know exactly.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): How much blood is there? Are you soaking a pad?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): No, just when I wipe. Sort of brown, sometimes a bit pink. Not filling a pad or anything.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any clots in it?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No clots.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): And these cramps, where do you feel them, and how bad?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Low in my tummy, like a period, comes and goes. Not agony. Maybe a four out of ten. I don't know.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any pain at the tip of your shoulder?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you had a fever, or actually been sick?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): No fever. I feel queasy but I haven't vomited.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any stinging when you pass water?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): I hardly slept last night. I was on my phone looking things up till gone two. Stupid, really.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Very easy to do that. The waterworks though, any burning?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Oh, sorry. No, that's been normal.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright. Brown spotting since about Thursday, period-type cramps low down, nausea without vomiting, no clots, no shoulder pain. What medicines are you on?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): Folic acid, the little yellow tablets, for the pregnancy. Four hundred micrograms, one by mouth each day. And I've had a headache on and off, so I've been taking Crocin.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Crocin, that's paracetamol, yes? What strength are the tablets?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): I think five hundred milligrams. I'm not sure, doctor. The box is at home.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the folic acid, are you taking it every day?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Most days. I forget some mornings if I'm rushing for the bus. I don't know how many I've missed.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any allergies, medicines or otherwise?
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't think so. Nothing I can remember. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is this your first pregnancy?
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes. We'd been trying. I came off Microgynon, the contraceptive pill, back in the summer.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any operations, or long-term illnesses? And do you smoke, or drink?
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Appendix out when I was sixteen. Nothing else ongoing. I don't smoke. I packed in the drinking when the test went positive.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): That was a home test, or the chemist?
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): Chemist one. Two lines, clear. That was, I don't know, a few weeks back. I can't remember the day.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Would you like your partner in? I can get the nurse.
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes please. He's been wearing a hole in the floor out there.
[SEG0040] person_1 (NURSE): I'll fetch him now.
[SEG0041] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, sorry. The car park machine ate my change and I got in a strop about it. Hi. Is everything alright?
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): We're still piecing it together. She's had spotting and some cramp. From your side, how long has the bleeding been going on?
[SEG0043] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Longer than four days. It was there last weekend at her mum's. That's more like ten days, if I'm honest.
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): Was it? I don't know, doctor. I only properly noticed on Thursday. He might be right, though. I can't swear to it.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then we won't force a single number. I'll record roughly four to ten days, and leave it uncertain. Has she seemed faint to you?
[SEG0046] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yesterday she nearly fainted. Properly pale, had to sit down on the stairs.
[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): I did not faint. I was just tired. I don't know why he's saying fainted.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll note tiredness, and that the two of you don't agree about fainting. Any family history, pregnancies that ran into trouble?
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): My sister had a pregnancy outside the womb, years ago. That's all I can think about.
[SEG0050] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the penicillin thing. Your mum always said you swelled up with it when you were little.
[SEG0051] person_3 (PATIENT): Did I? I've never been told it properly. I don't think I'm allergic. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll flag penicillin as mentioned but not confirmed, and we simply won't use it today. May I feel your tummy?
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): Soft. A little tender low down in the middle. No guarding, and you're not rigid. I won't do an internal examination.

[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thinking aloud, the possibilities I have in mind are a threatened miscarriage, some harmless implantation bleeding, or, less often, a pregnancy outside the womb. I am not concluding any of those. I can't, not yet.
[SEG0055] person_3 (PATIENT): So it might be the bad one. I don't know if I can sit with that.

[SEG0056] person_2 (DOCTOR): It might be any of those, and it might turn out milder than you fear. What we will do today is a scan, plus bloods: a pregnancy hormone level, a full blood count, and your blood group. The nurse will get those done.
[SEG0057] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the bleeding does not settle, we might repeat the scan in a fortnight. I'm not booking that now.
[SEG0058] person_3 (PATIENT): And if it gets worse tonight, what do I do? I don't know, doctor.

[SEG0059] person_2 (DOCTOR): If you soak a pad inside an hour, the pain turns severe, you feel faint, or the shoulder tip starts hurting, go straight to A&E and don't wait for clinic. Otherwise I'll see you back here in one week with the results.
[SEG0060] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Should she be off work?

[SEG0061] person_2 (DOCTOR): Light duties if your job allows, and avoid intercourse until the spotting stops. Keep swallowing the folic acid even on rough mornings. Paracetamol, your Crocin, is fine for the headache, but don't guess at other painkillers.
[SEG0062] person_3 (PATIENT): Is there something for the sickness? The mornings are grim.
[SEG0063] person_2 (DOCTOR): We might add an anti-sickness tablet if the nausea isn't easing in a few days. I won't start one today.
[SEG0064] person_3 (PATIENT): I just want the baby to be okay. I don't know, doctor. That's the whole of it.
[SEG0065] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We both do. Forget the car park, that was a daft way to walk in.

[SEG0066] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me say it back. Early pregnancy, dates uncertain around Diwali, spotting for somewhere between four and ten days, mild low cramps, some nausea and a headache, folic acid most days, Crocin possibly five hundred milligrams, penicillin not clear. Scan and bloods today, a repeat scan only if the bleeding doesn't settle, and back in a week unless you need A&E.
[SEG0067] person_1 (NURSE): I can take you for the bloods now, and the scan is this afternoon, about half two. Your partner can sit with you.
[SEG0068] person_3 (PATIENT): Half two. Thank you. I don't know how I'll keep still till then, but yes.

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
